title_en: Measures on Disciplinary Punishment for Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Measures for Disciplinary Sanctions in the Enforcement Work of People's Courts (Trial Implementation)

(Adopted at the 1243rd Meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on September 12, 2002, and effective as of the date of promulgation)

Fa Fa [2002] No. 15

To ensure the fairness and efficiency of enforcement work and to promote the integrity-building of the People's Courts, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws.

Article 1. Where a staff member of a People's Court, in the course of enforcement work, intentionally violates relevant laws or regulations, or negligently violates relevant laws or regulations causing serious consequences, the matter shall be handled in accordance with these Measures.

Article 2. Where a staff member intentionally violates the provisions of the law by failing to accept an enforcement case that should be accepted, or by illegally accepting an enforcement application that should not be accepted, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Where, due to negligence, an enforcement case that should be accepted according to law is not accepted, or an enforcement application that should not be accepted is illegally accepted, causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 3. Where a staff member intentionally violates the relevant provisions of the Measures on Litigation Fees of the People's Courts by unilaterally exceeding the standard or scope in collecting enforcement fees, thereby causing adverse effects, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 4. Where a staff member, knowing there are statutory grounds for withdrawal, fails to withdraw on his or her own initiative according to law, thereby causing adverse effects, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 5. Where a staff member gives advance notice to a person subject to enforcement or an assistant in enforcement, thereby enabling the person to abscond or to transfer, conceal, or sell off the property subject to enforcement, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 6. Where a staff member intentionally delays or fails to enforce a case that meets the conditions for enforcement, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Where, due to negligence, enforcement is delayed, causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 7. Where a staff member, as required by relevant provisions, fails to take action to investigate, search, seal up, distrain, freeze, or sell off the property of the person subject to enforcement, or fails to entrust relevant institutions with auditing, appraisal, or auction, thereby causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to demotion.

Article 8. Where a staff member, in the course of compulsory enforcement, fails to present the court staff's identification and relevant legal documents according to law, thereby causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 9. Where a staff member intentionally violates the provisions of the law by adopting compulsory measures such as summoning for detention, detention, or fines against the person subject to enforcement, assistant in enforcement, or other persons, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Where there is negligence in the adoption of compulsory measures, causing serious consequences such as casualties, the sanction shall be a warning up to discharge.

Article 10. Where a staff member intentionally seals up, distrains, freezes, or sells off the severable property of the person subject to enforcement in excess of the subject matter of the claim, causing significant losses, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion or removal from office.

Article 11. Where a staff member unilaterally releases property that has been sealed up, distrained, or frozen, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion or removal from office.

Article 12. Where a staff member intentionally violates the provisions of the law by erroneously changing or adding to the person subject to enforcement, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Where, due to negligence, the provisions of the law are violated by erroneously changing or adding to the person subject to enforcement, causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 13. Where a staff member fails to examine and handle according to law an objection raised by a third party regarding the subject matter of enforcement, thereby causing property losses to the third party, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 14. Where a staff member, for the purpose of seeking personal gain or subjectively favoring one party, intentionally violates the provisions of the law by forcing the other party to reach a settlement agreement in enforcement against its true will, thereby harming its interests, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 15. Where a staff member, for the purpose of seeking personal gain or for the benefit of one party, violates relevant provisions by engaging in fraud in the selection of intermediary institutions such as auditing, appraisal, auction, or evaluation institutions, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Where a staff member accepts money, goods, or other benefits from the aforementioned intermediary institutions, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 16. Where a staff member instructs or suggests relevant departments or personnel to intentionally lower or raise prices in violation of relevant provisions during appraisal or auction, thereby harming the interests of the parties, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 17. Where a staff member intentionally violates the provisions of the law by suspending, staying, or terminating enforcement, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 18. Where a staff member intentionally violates the provisions of the law by failing to resume enforcement of a case that should be resumed, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 19. Where a staff member intentionally violates the results of collegial panel deliberations or the decision of the adjudication committee in preparing enforcement documents, the sanction shall be a major demerit up to discharge.

Where, due to negligence, errors occur in the content of enforcement documents prepared, causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 20. Where a staff member forges or falsifies enforcement documents, the sanction shall be a major demerit up to discharge.

Article 21. Where a staff member intentionally damages or conceals case files or evidentiary materials, the sanction shall be a major demerit up to discharge.

Where case files or evidentiary materials are lost, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 22. Where a staff member fails to serve enforcement documents according to law, causing serious consequences, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 23. Where a staff member intentionally violates relevant provisions by enforcing a claim of the person subject to enforcement that is due from a third party, thereby causing property losses to the third party, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 24. Where, in a case where multiple creditors file enforcement applications against a single debtor, a staff member colludes with a party and intentionally violates the procedures and principles for distribution among creditors, thereby harming the interests of other parties, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 25. Where a staff member, without justifiable reasons, intentionally delays the return of enforcement proceeds or other property to a creditor, thereby causing losses to the creditor, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 26. Where a staff member intentionally pays enforcement proceeds to another party, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if losses are caused to the creditor, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Where, due to negligence, enforcement proceeds are paid to another party, causing losses to the creditor, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 27. Where a staff member intentionally delays or refuses to execute an enforcement decision of a higher people's court, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if serious consequences are caused, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 28. Where a staff member, without justifiable reasons, intentionally delays or fails to enforce a case entrusted by a people's court of another locality that meets the conditions for enforcement, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 29. Where a staff member accepts money, goods, or other benefits from a party or its agent, or requires a party or its agent to reimburse expenses that should be borne by the staff member personally, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 30. Where a staff member accepts invitations to meals from a party or its agent, or participates in entertainment or other activities paid for by the party or its agent, thereby causing adverse effects, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit.

Article 31. Where a staff member, taking advantage of enforcement work, borrows money, goods, or other property from a party or its agent for personal use, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 32. Where a staff member uses, intercepts, misappropriates, embezzles, or secretly distributes enforcement proceeds of a case and their interest or other property, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 33. Where a staff member, taking advantage of enforcement work, seeks improper benefits for himself or herself, his or her spouse, children, or other persons, the sanction shall be a warning up to a major demerit; if the circumstances are serious, the sanction shall be demotion up to discharge.

Article 34. Where a violation of these Measures is minor, the person responsible shall be ordered to make a self-criticism or be subject to a circular criticism.

Article 35. Where a violation of these Measures is suspected of constituting a crime, the matter shall be transferred to the relevant judicial authority after disciplinary sanctions are imposed, or disciplinary sanctions shall be imposed after the matter is dealt with by the relevant judicial authority.

Article 36. These Measures shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 37. These Measures shall enter into force as of the date of promulgation.

September 25, 2002
